newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean Kim's associate, MP arrested over Hanbo.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean Kim's associate, MP arrested over Hanbo.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors said they arrested on Tuesday a close associate of President Kim Young-sam and a top ruling party official in connection with huge loans to the failed Hanbo Steel Co.

The arrest of Hong In-gil, a senior official at the presidential Blue House until a few months before he was elected to parliament last year, and Chung Jae-chull, the highest ranking New Korea Party official after Kim and party chairman Lee Hong-koo, was broadcast by state television.

Hong and Chung were charged with accepting kickbacks from founder Chung Tae-soo of the Hanbo Group, whose steelmaking flagship racked up five trillion won ($5.8 billion) in loans before being declared insolvent on January 23, a prosecution official said.
They are the first politicians to be arrested over the loan scandal that has shocked South Korea and put the heat on Kim in a presidential election year.
The Hanbo tycoon has already been arrested on charges of fraud and other violations. Two leading local bankers have also been arrested on charges of bribery.
President Kim last month ordered a probe into the loans and has called the scandal a typical example of corruption.
